newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian plane crash flight data recovered.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian plane crash flight data recovered.

text.p: Indonesian authorities have recovered the flight data and cockpit voice recorders of a plane which crashed on the island of Belitung, killing at least 15 people, the official Antara news agency reported on Sunday.

Investigations were continuing into Saturday's crash of Merpati Nusantara Airlines' twin-engined British Aerospace Advanced Turbo Prop (ATP) plane at Belitung, 400 km (250 miles) north of Jakarta, Antara quoted the airline's operations director Prasetjo Witjaksono Sembodo as saying.
The 68-seat plane with 48 passengers and five crew on board crashed into a coconut plantation on approach to Belitung's Buluh Tumbang airport after leaving Jakarta earlier in the day.

"The flight recorder of the ill-fated plane has already been found and on Monday the investigating team will meet to discuss the sending of the black-box to the United Kingdom or Australia," Prasetjo told reporters on Saturday night.
The Kompas daily newspaper reported on Sunday that the cockpit voice recorder would be analysed in Indonesia.
Prasetjo said the pilot had radioed the airport control tower four minutes before the crash saying the plane was at an altitude of 2,500 feet (800 metres) and ready to land.
Kompas quoted the Director General of Air Transport, Zainuddin Sikado, as saying all ATP aircraft operated by Merpati would be grounded until the cause of the crash was known.
It quoted local transport department officials as saying the weather at Belitung was good at the time of the accident and visibility was normal.
An administrative official at Belitung's general hospital told Reuters on Sunday the death toll remained at 15 and the 31 people injured would be flown to Jakarta for further treatment.
Merpati released a full passenger list but could not immediately identify all the dead, except for the 28-year-old pilot, his co-pilot and a stewardess.
